faq.title: FAQ
faq.desc: Pooling, transparent failover, credential storage and quota domains.
faq.keywords: faq why is how secure credential storage quota

concept-route.title: Route
concept-route.body: A route is the single entry point backed by a pool of upstream accounts. Scripts only know the address the route exposes — not which account or region serves them. Routes belong to their creator: even an admin only sees their own routes.

concept-provider-key.title: Provider credential
concept-provider-key.body: One provider credential is one upstream account, with its endpoint, model list and inbound formats. All credentials under a route serve together; the gateway picks one by the selection strategy and, when one is unavailable, switches accounts before the first byte so scripts never notice.
concept-provider-key.keywords: provider credential upstream account model selection

concept-api-key.title: API key
concept-api-key.body: An API key is the caller's credential, bound to one route. Scripts use it to reach the gateway. The plaintext is shown exactly once at creation; afterwards only the mask and prefix are visible.
concept-api-key.keywords: api key secret caller plaintext mask

concept-quota-domain.title: Quota domain
concept-quota-domain.body: The quota domain is the unit of pooling: the quota of one upstream account belongs to a domain, and a key is merely that domain's credential. The same account can therefore serve several routes, while usage is still attributed per call.

task-create-route.title: Create a route
task-create-route.body: Use the plus next to “Routes” in the sidebar, or “New” in the empty state. Name is required, description optional; saving takes you straight to the route detail page.

task-add-provider.title: Add upstream accounts
task-add-provider.body: Open the route detail page and click “New” in the provider section: pick a preset (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, …), paste the upstream credential, adjust inbound formats if needed. Saving fetches the model list automatically.
task-add-provider.keywords: add upstream provider preset credential models

task-create-key.title: Create an API key
task-create-key.body: On the API keys page click “New”, choose the route, set a name and expiry. The plaintext is shown once — copy it into your script or a password manager before closing.

task-rotate-key.title: Rotate an API key
task-rotate-key.body: Create the new key on the same route first, switch the script over and confirm calls succeed, then delete the old key. Never delete before creating — the gap breaks the script.
task-rotate-key.keywords: rotate change key migrate rolling delete

task-disable-route.title: Disable a route temporarily
task-disable-route.body: Turn off the switch at the top of the route detail page: it stops forwarding while keeping config and credentials. Flip it back to resume. Use “Archive” only when you are done for good.

trouble-401.title: 401: credential invalid
trouble-401.body: A 401 from upstream means the credential is unusable. The gateway treats it as permanent retirement and quarantines the account: it stops participating in selection and needs manual recovery. Once the upstream account works again, an admin clicks “Clear” in the health column on the route page.

trouble-403.title: 403: account anomaly
trouble-403.body: A 403 only means this request was rejected — it does not prove the account is banned. The gateway treats the account as temporarily unavailable and fails over: it cools down while other credentials serve, then rejoins selection automatically.

trouble-cooldown.title: Everything is cooling down
trouble-cooldown.body: Cooldown durations live in “System → Gateway”. If every credential is cooling down, check upstream rate limits or exhausted quota; the health column shows when the longest cooldown ends.

trouble-no-model.title: Model list empty or not probeable
trouble-no-model.body: Without a model list the gateway can neither probe health nor route traffic. Edit the provider and click “Fetch models”, or add a model mapping manually.

trouble-tls.title: Certificate not ready
trouble-tls.body: “System → HTTPS” shows the certificate state. Waiting usually means DNS or ports 80 / 443 are not reachable; paused means issuance hit its limit — fix the cause and click “Retry”.
trouble-tls.keywords: certificate tls https acme issue port domain

faq-switch.title: Where does “transparent failover” end?
faq-switch.body: It is guaranteed only before the first byte: switching accounts before any response byte reaches the script is invisible. If upstream dies after the stream started, the gateway will not splice two responses — the script sees an error and must retry.
faq-switch.keywords: transparent failover first byte streaming retry

faq-tls.title: Is TLS mandatory?
faq-tls.body: Not for a purely internal deployment. Once employee scripts or terminal agents reach the gateway over a public network it is required, otherwise API keys travel in plaintext in every request header.
faq-tls.keywords: tls https required public network plaintext security

faq-credentials.title: Where are upstream credentials stored?
faq-credentials.body: In the local SQLite database (`solidway.db` under `data_root`), with sensitive fields encrypted using `master.key`. The console only ever shows masks.
faq-credentials.keywords: credential storage encryption master key database sqlite privacy

faq-quota.title: Can several employees share one upstream account?
faq-quota.body: Yes — that is the point of pooling. The account belongs to a quota domain; each employee uses an API key on their own route, and usage is attributed per call.
faq-quota.keywords: share account pooling multiple users attribution

faq-scripts.title: What do existing scripts need to change?
faq-scripts.body: Usually two fields: `base_url` pointing at the gateway, and `api_key` set to the key the gateway issued. Protocol families are not translated.
faq-scripts.keywords: script migrate base url api key compatible zero change

faq-delete.title: Disable vs. archive vs. delete
faq-delete.body: Disable keeps config but stops forwarding; archive removes it from lists and the sidebar, makes the detail read-only and cannot be undone; API keys and provider credentials can be deleted for real.
